about: Where the graph of Storm Charles, Lisbon: Wednesday 11 November 2026 joins the site's other graphs, without copying them: the register of sources (sources/), the weather data supply chain (meteorology/) and our dated captures (evidence/, Wayback). Each edge runs from a node of data/graph/storm.json to "<world>/<that world's own id>", with the page to open (href, relative to the site), a label, a source, the time read, where it was built from, and why. "captures" holds, once per address this graph was read at, our latest capture of it (evidence/<id>.html) or the reason there is none. The verbs and their inverses: data/graph/ontology.json, crossings. Built by tools/graph-build.mjs, never by hand. Not a warning service: follow IPMA and ANEPC.

entities.what: Everything a page can mention, with a page each (incident.entities@).
entities.joined_by: its `graph` field names this graph's node; the node carries `entity`

sources.what: The register of outside bodies this site takes data from or cites, with each licence as published (incident.sources@).
sources.joined_by: its `entity` field, through entities/index.json; otherwise one of its hosts

meteorology.what: The weather data supply chain: bodies, observing systems, models, datasets, warning services and sites, with its own ten verbs (incident.meteorology@).
meteorology.joined_by: the joins it states on its own nodes: `entity` (the same thing), `of` (who publishes a site), `source` (the register's id); a body with none of these, by the host of its address

evidence.what: Wayback: our own dated captures of outside pages and feeds (incident.archivist@).
